problem: Generative (diffusion) policies can hallucinate future decisions when the goal is not fully observable, and conventional RL/IL or modular pipelines struggle to follow language instructions under partial observability.
motivation: Embodied agents must follow language instructions while the target is often not visible at the start. Existing diffusion planners such as Decision Diffuser do not explicitly model language and their behavior under uncertainty is an open question. The paper jointly predicts a belief goal and the plan, and re-plans as new observations arrive.
key_idea: Treat planning as in-painting: a language-conditioned diffusion model denoises a state-trajectory channel and a goal-estimation channel on a 2D task feature map, and an on-the-fly loop re-plans after each executed step.
insight: The ablation on CompILE P-MO2G shows the goal-estimation channel g lifts SR from 6.90 to 28.60, and on-the-fly re-planning lifts it further to 99.89. One-shot and two-shot planning reach only 28.6 and 54.7, so re-planning with newly revealed information is what resolves the uncertainty. Language must be an explicit condition, since DD without language falls far behind on Kuka, and the authors also report a performance drop when using classifier-free guidance.
method: Planning space: x in R^{H×W×(C+T+1)} concatenates the task feature map o_t (C channels) with T future state-map channels and 1 goal-estimation channel; only the last T+1 channels are noised and generated, like image in-painting.
Joint plan and goal modeling: p(τ,g|o,I)=p(τ|g,o,I)p(g|o,I); the diffusion model predicts the trajectory and a belief goal state together to reduce hallucination under partial observability.

Diffusion training: a UNet2DConditionModel predicts the noise, conditioned on the feature map (as input channels) and instruction text via cross-attention (CLIP text embeddings). DDIM with a cosine schedule and 100 diffusion steps; no classifier-free guidance.
On-the-fly planning: at each step, denoise from scratch, execute only the first predicted state, observe the new environment and re-plan, until termination.
Inverse-dynamics execution: a_t = ψ(s_t, s_{t+1}) converts consecutive predicted states into actions (A* for grid/navigation, inverse kinematics for the Kuka arm).
Task feature maps: BERT/CLIP embeddings per grid cell for CompILE, block positions for Kuka, and a FILM-style 2D semantic map (48×48) for ALFRED, on which the planner replaces FILM's planning.

setting.backbone: Conditional UNet diffusion model (UNet2DConditionModel, trained from scratch) with CLIP text encoder; on ALFRED built on FILM's modular perception pipeline
setting.training_data: Ground-truth expert trajectories from A* on CompILE, Kuka demonstrations with template instructions, and ALFRED expert data; 200 epochs, batch size 64
setting.observation: 2D top-down task feature maps (grid object embeddings, block positions, FILM semantic map from egocentric RGB + estimated depth)
setting.action_space: Predicted state (position) trajectories decoded by an inverse dynamics model (A* or inverse kinematics), i.e. FILM-style discrete actions on ALFRED
setting.simulator: CompILE grid world, Kuka block-stacking, ALFRED (AI2-THOR)
setting.privileged: none stated (ALFRED uses learned detection and depth like FILM)

numbers_note: Paper evaluates on CompILE, Kuka and ALFRED, none of which are among the canonical navigation benchmarks. ALFRED is canonical but it is an instruction-following/task-planning benchmark and its numbers are given below in the results and in evidence rather than as VLN benchmark entries. ALFRED results are SR/path-weighted SR and GC/path-weighted GC; the numbers list is left empty because the metrics do not map cleanly to the schema.
results: On ALFRED, planning improves unseen-environment SR from 20.4 to 26.1 (validation) and 22.2 to 24.7 (test, FILM re-run best of five) over FILM, though it is below EmBERT and E.T. on seen validation. On CompILE it reaches 99.5 to 99.9 SR across settings versus BC/CQL, which are at or below 23.2 in the multi-object settings, and on Kuka it reaches 98 to 99.8 versus the strongest baseline DD at 58 to 67.2.
limitations: Planning space is 2D, which limits applicability to environments needing 3D spatial reasoning.
Performance drops with diverse, complex instructions (Kuka rearrange multi-constraint falls from 98.85 to 78.55; ALFRED gains are modest).
On-the-fly planning is slow because diffusion restarts from scratch at every step.
